hook_text: In 1991 a superpower with thousands of nuclear weapons disappeared without losing a single war.
clip_script: The Soviet Union. Fifteen republics, nearly 290 million people, held together by one party, one army and one secret police. Then Gorbachev loosens the grip. People start to speak. In the Baltic states, two million hold hands in a chain hundreds of kilometres long. Freedom, they say. The shops empty. Prices rise. August 1991: hardliners lock Gorbachev in his holiday house and send tanks into Moscow. But Boris Yeltsin climbs onto a tank and calls on the people to resist. Crowds build barricades. Soldiers refuse to shoot. Three days later the plot collapses. Now the republics walk away, one by one. Ukraine votes to leave. On Christmas night, 1991, Gorbachev resigns on television, and the red flag comes down over the Kremlin. Fifteen countries stand where one superpower stood.
visual_style: A map of the Soviet Union breaking into fifteen coloured pieces; a human chain of people holding hands across a countryside; tanks in a Moscow street; a man reading a statement on top of a tank; a red flag being lowered over a domed building in the dark.
pacing: Steady through the crisis, fast during the coup, slow and quiet as the flag comes down.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand why the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
